paragraphs: Rav Yitzḥak bar Shemuel bar Marta (see his entry). R. Abba said: R. Yitzḥak bar Shemuel bar Marta [said]. Rav Ahila, or Rav Aḥai, arranged his son's marriage into R. Yitzḥak bar Shemuel bar Marta's household. He asked Rav Huna, Ketubbot (21b). In chapter Kol Sha'ah (33, end of side b): Rava said: The house of R. Yitzḥak bar Marta said in Rav Huna’s name. In my opinion it should read 'R. Yitzḥak bar Shemuel bar Marta said,' and 'Rava' is a scribal error. R. Zeira called him 'our teacher,' Ḥullin (30, beginning of side b). In Rav Yehudah’s name, he spoke before Rav Kahana, Niddah (26b). He sat before Rav Naḥman and said, etc.; he said to him, ‘Answer me, my master’ [עני מרי], chapter HaTodah (81, beginning of side a), and chapter HaShoḥet (35a). He sat before Rav Naḥman; he spoke in Rav's name, Gittin (13a, 63b), chapter Sheloshah She'akhlu (46a), Menaḥot (29, end of side b), Berakhot (3a). There, chapter 2 (13b): R. Ila bar Rav Shemuel bar Marta, in Rav's name; so too in Asheri. In Rif, however, the reading is Rav Yitzḥak bar Shemuel bar Marta. This seems correct, for Rav Ila is a scribal error: no further mention of him is found. In the Shas, Pesaḥim (106b), he said, 'Rav has not yet died, and we have forgotten his teachings! Many times I stood before Rav.' Rabbah, in his name, Megillah (16b). Rami bar Ḥama raises an objection; he said to him, etc., chapter HaShoḥet (35a). He went down to Netzivin and found Simlai of Lod expounding: ‘Rav and his court permitted oil’ [the cited Bavli reads ‘R. Yehudah and his court’] (see above, R. Yehudah Nesia), Avodah Zarah (36a).
